topic: The Magic of Planar Graphs: Duality and Euler's Characteristic
target_audience: University students (Computer Science or Discrete Mathematics)

sections.title: Prerequisites: What is a Planar Graph?
lecture_lines: Planar graphs are drawn without edge crossings.
Key components are Vertices, Edges, and Faces.
Untangle crossings to reveal planar embeddings.
animations: Create a simple node and edge structure labeled 'G'. Use color #FF6600 for nodes. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]
Add an edge such that it crosses another, highlighting non-planarity. Color the crossing #FF0000.
Redraw the same structure without any crossing edges. Color nodes #00FF00.
Label the new planar layout as 'Planar Embedding'. Use color #FFFFFF.
Fade all elements to highlight the shift from non-planar to planar. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg]

sections.title: Euler’s Characteristic Formula
lecture_lines: Euler's formula states V - E + F = 2.
This holds for any connected planar graph.
The exterior region counts as one face.
Example: A triangle has V=3, E=3, F=2.
animations: Display the formula V - E + F = 2 in white (#FFFFFF). Label it 'Euler's Formula'. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/triangle.svg]
Introduce a small graph with 4 vertices, 6 edges, 4 faces. Color vertices #FF6600.
Highlight Faces F=4 in blue (#0000FF), then show the final calculation 4-6+4=2. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/triangle.svg]

sections.title: The Concept of Duality
lecture_lines: The dual graph G* transforms graph properties.
Place a node in each graph face.
Connect nodes sharing an edge boundary.
Honeycomb duals form a triangular lattice.
Duality shifts perspective to graph faces.
animations: Draw a graph G with vertices and edges in #FF6600, using [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/honeycomb.svg] as the structural template.
Place a dot in each face of G to represent dual vertices, colored #00FFFF.

Connect dual vertices across edges of G to form dual graph G*. Color edges of G* in #FFFF00, completing the dual transformation of [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/honeycomb.svg].

sections.title: Synthesis: Why Duality Works
lecture_lines: Vertices in G* correspond to faces in G.
Dual edges cross original edges perpendicularly.
Duality simplifies complex network path problems.
animations: Animate the dual transformation: vertices of G become faces of G*. Color #FF6600 to #00FFFF.
Show how edges crossing between G and G* remain orthogonal. Color intersections #FFFFFF.
Summarize: Planarity in G corresponds to planarity in G*. Highlight final conclusion in gold (#FFD700).

sections.title: Conclusion and Application
lecture_lines: Euler's formula verifies map coloring rules.
Duality optimizes network redundancy and routing.
Master duality to simplify graph theory problems.
animations: Show a real-world map [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/map.svg] with countries as nodes. Color regions #3399FF.
Convert the map [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/map.svg] to a planar graph overlay. Use #FFFFFF for edges.
